name: Rosemary

companions.note: Rosemary repels cabbage moth; good brassica companion
Rosemary scent confuses carrot fly; classic companion planting pair
Compatible drought-tolerant companions; similar sun and drainage needs

pnw_notes: Blue Lagoon is a trailing/prostrate rosemary — spreads along the ground rather than growing upright, beautiful at bed edges or cascading over a border. Evergreen in zone 8b under most winters; if temps drop below 15°F, drape with fleece overnight. Very drought tolerant once established. Flavor is most intense on woody stems. Harvest by snipping stem tips — never strip a whole branch bare.

frost_hardiness.notes: Evergreen and hardy through typical Portland winters. May suffer dieback in hard freezes below 15°F — protect with fleece. Trim damaged tips in spring and the plant recovers quickly.

planting_windows.notes: Spring transplant preferred for best establishment
Fall transplant viable; roots establish well before first frost
Year-round harvest; harvest lightly first year while establishing
